name: Sierpiński space
description: Two-point set {0, 1} where the open sets are empty, {1}, and {0, 1}. The point 0 is not closed, so it is T0 but not T1.
source: Steen & Seebach, Counterexamples in Topology, Item 14 (Sierpinski Space)

name: Cofinite topology on an infinite set
description: An infinite set X with open sets being empty and all subsets with finite complement. Every singleton is closed, but no two disjoint open non-empty sets exist, failing Hausdorff (T2).
source: Steen & Seebach, Counterexamples in Topology, Item 18 (Countable Fort Space / Cofinite Topology); Munkres §17 Ex. 3

name: Tychonoff plank
description: The subspace [0, omega_1] x [0, omega] \ {(omega_1, omega)}. Completely regular (T3 1/2) as a subspace of a compact Hausdorff space, but fails normality (T4).
source: Steen & Seebach, Counterexamples in Topology, Item 86 (Tychonoff Plank); Willard §17

name: Sorgenfrey plane
description: Product of two Sorgenfrey lines R_l x R_l. The Sorgenfrey line R_l is normal and Lindelöf, but its square R_l x R_l is completely regular and first countable while failing normality (the anti-diagonal contains an uncountable closed discrete subset).
source: Steen & Seebach, Counterexamples in Topology, Item 84; Munkres §31 Ex. 3

name: [0, 1]^R (Uncountable cube)
description: Product of uncountably many copies of [0, 1]. Compact by Tychonoff's theorem, but not first countable and not sequentially compact (no subsequence of the sequence of coordinate projections converges).
source: Steen & Seebach, Counterexamples in Topology, Item 105; Munkres §28 Theorem 28.2 / §38

name: omega_1 (First uncountable ordinal)
description: The set of countable ordinals [0, omega_1) with the order topology. It is sequentially compact and countably compact, but not compact (the open cover by intervals [0, alpha) has no finite subcover) and not Lindelöf.
source: Steen & Seebach, Counterexamples in Topology, Item 42; Munkres §28 Example 2
